items.title: A characterisation of affine formal algebraic spaces by thickenings from affine schemes

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises a sheaf on the fppf site being an affine formal algebraic space by two conditions: that every morphism from an affine scheme factors through a representable thickening from an affine scheme, and a set-theoretic condition recalled from a remark (statement lines 2095-2106). One direction follows from two earlier statements of the chapter. For the converse the proof builds the presentation explicitly: the category of representable thickenings from affine schemes is shown to be directed, which uses that the coproduct of two such thickenings can be factored through a third and that between any two objects there is at most one arrow, and the sheaf is written as the colimit over that category, which by hypothesis is a filtered colimit of affine schemes (proof lines 2108-2122). It remains to see that the transition arrows in that presentation are thickenings, which is proved by writing a thickening as a fibre product with itself over the target and using that the target is a monomorphism of sheaves (proof lines 2122-2126). The claim is H2: the two properties defining the presentation -- directedness of the index category and the fact that its arrows are thickenings -- are each verified, the second by a short fibre product computation.
